10:30-12:30.label: Build, debug, or solve a problem

12:30-14:00.label: Role research and tailored application work
12:30-14:00.output: Verified role scorecard or application evidence

14:30-16:30.label: Open source or public portfolio proof

20:30-21:30.label: Follow-up, outreach, and next-day review

days.mission: Activate the system: audit your resume and portfolio, confirm the first target role, study the assigned chapter, and finish one practice artifact that is feasible from the current time. Earlier blocks today are not overdue.
days.practiceTask: Implement one user-facing interaction and check keyboard, loading, empty, and error states. Day 1: explain the decision and attach a commit, diagram, or recording.
days.interviewQuestion: Explain Execution Context to a senior interviewer. State the invariant, one failure mode, one trade-off, and how you would verify the result.
interviewQuestions: Explain Execution Context to a senior interviewer. State the invariant, one failure mode, one trade-off, and how you would verify the result.

ossTrack.action: Read the contribution guide and map the local architecture; do not open a speculative PR.

roleTrack.action: Select one Germany role; verify the exact opening, language, location, and qualifying-offer/visa conditions from its source.

days.mockInterviewPlatform: micro1 free AI mock or Exponent/Pramp peer practice; recorded self-review every day
days.founderOutreachTarget: At most one relevant follow-up or warm conversation; quality before volume
steps: Open each assigned chapter from study.buildora.work and note its main invariant: Execution Context; Scope; Call Stack; Hoisting.
Close the reading tab and write the recall answer before checking your notes.
Complete the practice task in a small branch or isolated exercise; run the relevant tests and capture the result.
Verify one Germany or remote role from its exact listing and save its source, eligibility, evidence match, and gap.
Follow the OSS rule for Langfuse: confirm scope with maintainers before coding; if no agreed issue exists, ship a public proof artifact instead.
Record a timed interview answer, score clarity/technical depth/trade-offs, and write one correction.
Use the final checklist to attach evidence, verify completed outputs, and carry unfinished work into a dated next action.

checklist.text: Write concise notes for today's assigned chapters
checklist.acceptanceCriteria: At least 5 accurate ideas, one worked example, one open question, and links to the assigned chapters.
instructions: Read the linked chapters and capture definitions only when they help explain a mechanism.
For each chapter, write its invariant, one small example, and one failure mode.
Add one question you still have and keep the note in the matching project or study folder.

checklist.text: Explain one chapter concept from memory
checklist.acceptanceCriteria: A 2–5 minute recording or written answer created before reopening notes, covering mechanism, trade-off, failure mode, and a verification method.
instructions: Choose one assigned chapter and close the chapter and notes.
Explain the concept from first principles, then name a realistic failure and a way to test for it.
Reopen the source, mark what was missing, and record one correction for tomorrow.

checklist.text: Complete the applied engineering exercise
checklist.acceptanceCriteria: A reproducible commit or runnable artifact with a focused test and a short explanation of the design trade-off.
instructions: Use this exercise: Implement one user-facing interaction and check keyboard, loading, empty, and error states. Day 1: explain the decision and attach a commit, diagram, or recording.
Reduce it to the smallest useful change that demonstrates today's chapter in a realistic feature.
Run the relevant test or command, inspect the result, and capture a commit URL/hash or runnable artifact.
Write down one alternative you rejected and why.

checklist.text: Complete today's role research or application action
checklist.acceptanceCriteria: Company, exact live role URL, source-check date, location/work-authorisation eligibility, resume-backed evidence match, gap, and next action are recorded.
instructions: Select one Germany role; verify the exact opening, language, location, and qualifying-offer/visa conditions from its source.
Open the employer's own listing and confirm it is still accepting applications; record the checked date and location/work-authorisation constraints.
Match each required skill to an existing resume or portfolio example; label missing evidence honestly.
Save one next action as a draft. Submit only after reviewing the final application yourself.

checklist.text: Make progress on OSS or public proof
checklist.acceptanceCriteria: A public issue/discussion, reviewed artifact, or portfolio link; if blocked, save the maintainer question and a useful fallback proof artifact.
instructions: Follow today's Langfuse scope: Read the contribution guide and map the local architecture; do not open a speculative PR.
Read the contribution guide and issue discussion before editing; ask maintainers to confirm ambiguous scope.
Keep the change narrow, add or run relevant tests, and link the discussion, PR, or published proof.
If waiting on a maintainer, record the question and use the block for a portfolio proof instead.

checklist.text: Practice today's interview question under a timer
checklist.acceptanceCriteria: A 5–10 minute timed answer that states assumptions, reasoning, trade-offs, failure handling, verification, and one correction for the next attempt.
instructions: Answer the day's question without notes for up to 10 minutes.
Use a clear structure: clarify, state the invariant, compare options, cover failure modes, and explain verification.
Replay or review the answer, score clarity and technical depth, then write one specific correction.

checklist.text: Complete the evening review and set up tomorrow
checklist.acceptanceCriteria: Completed evidence is checked, unfinished work has a dated next action, one lesson is captured, and tomorrow's first task is selected.
instructions: Verify every claimed completion against its acceptance criteria and attached evidence.
Carry unfinished work forward as one small, dated next action; do not mark it complete.
Write one lesson from today and choose the first chapter or task to open tomorrow.

notifications.message: Day 1: start with health, then open today's roadmap.
Close the study block with notes and recall for Day 1.
Save today's verified role scorecard or application evidence.
Start the timed mock and capture one improvement.
Protect the two-hour family block; work resumes at 20:30.
Verify today's evidence and set the first task for tomorrow.
